hints.title: Ordered Body Coordinate Queue
hints.text: The moving snake advances its leading head cell while conditionally retracting its trailing tail position upon non-food steps.

hints.title: Tail Eviction and Collision Verification
hints.text: When stepping forward, pop the tail first before testing boundary limits or self-intersection, because moving into the cell vacated by the tail is valid.

hints.title: Movement State Blueprint
hints.text: Store body in a double-ended buffer and body cells in a hash set. Calculate new head coordinates. Check board bounds. Pop tail and remove from set. If new head in set, return -1. If food matches new head, consume food, re-add tail, increment score. Push new head and return score.

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```python
from collections import deque

class SnakeGame:
    def __init__(self, width: int, height: int, food: list[list[int]]):
        self.width = width
        self.height = height
        self.food = deque(food)
        self.body = deque([(0, 0)])
        self.body_set = {(0, 0)}
        self.score = 0
        self.directions = {'U': (-1, 0), 'D': (1, 0), 'L': (0, -1), 'R': (0, 1)}

    def move(self, direction: str) -> int:
        dr, dc = self.directions[direction]
        head_r, head_c = self.body[0]
        nr, nc = head_r + dr, head_c + dc

        if nr < 0 or nr >= self.height or nc < 0 or nc >= self.width:
            return -1

        tail = self.body.pop()
        self.body_set.remove(tail)

        if (nr, nc) in self.body_set:
            return -1

        if self.food and self.food[0] == [nr, nc]:
            self.food.popleft()
            self.body.append(tail)
            self.body_set.add(tail)
            self.score += 1

        self.body.appendleft((nr, nc))
        self.body_set.add((nr, nc))
        return self.score
```

complexity.notes: Each move executes in constant time using deque push/pop and set membership checks.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning the full snake body array on every step to detect collisions takes O(L) time where L is snake length.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Dual representations (deque for sequence, hash set for coordinates) guarantees O(1) step operations.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Correctly handling the case where the new head occupies the exact cell just vacated by the tail.
